recipe_rules.base_selection: base_records/base_envelopes are literal schema-3 canonical fixtures, signed only with the public fixture key. Use their matching reader_context, then apply the explicit case edits. No migration or hidden normalization is required.
recipe_rules.record: Sequential RFC-6901 pointer edits to deep copy; add creates object member, replace/remove require existing target; canonical serialize and HMAC AFTER edits.
recipe_rules.envelope: Sequential pointer edits to literal signed base envelope; canonical serialize envelope, never resign.
recipe_rules.raw: Canonical base envelope bytes then raw_transform; append ASCII spaces (byte 0x20) to exact total_bytes; replace_utf8 replaces entire response.
recipe_rules.record_raw: Canonical base record bytes; prefix_duplicate_key inserts literal JSON member after opening brace followed by comma; sign those exact bytes without reparsing.
recipe_rules.context: Named trusted test prerequisites, not wire fields. Integrity and transport labels are scenario facts, not real commissioning evidence. Restart reloads same state/pin; missing/corrupt never initializes.
recipe_rules.scope: Record refusal invalidates that source feed; component/activity refusal leaves independent components accepted; grammar-phase controls validate only the named isolated phase, never assert full-record acceptance. Acceptance controls prescribe PASS/FAIL criteria rather than one compound wire failure.
recipe_rules.acceptance: Predetermined not measured. Literal base envelopes carry fixture-key signatures, never host credentials or live receipts.
recipe_rules.verification_limit: Document validation may parse JSON, inspect recipe structure, canonical bytes and public fixture signatures. No proposed reader, classifier, collector, gate, verifier or host control is executed.

operation_order: Select the literal schema-3 base and named reader_context. Deep-copy both; case mutations are independent.

Apply case edits literally and in order. For record edits, canonical serialize and fixture-HMAC only after edits. For raw/envelope cases use the literal signed base envelope; never resign an envelope attack.

Ready/live contexts include a fresh independent authenticated verifier transaction at request-start 2026-10-11T12:00:20.500Z and answer/OK 12:00:21.000Z, uncertainty 0, fresh nonce, stable kernel/counter and participating lock. The committed snapshot matches the candidate only if its incarnation equals the trusted Pin. Historical/other-incarnation candidates do not change the current Pin. Cached-only contexts lack this transaction.

The verifier may authenticate committed malformed bytes; record validation still refuses grammar/provenance/semantics/time failures. Generation and sequence checks precede candidate snapshot equality; attacks never mutate trusted history or renew a lease.
